title: Kioxia CM10 Series Launched for the PCIe Gen6 Generation of SSDs
gist: Kioxia's CM10 series brings PCIe 6.0 and BiCS FLASH generation 10 to enterprise SSDs with direct-liquid-cooling EDSFF variants, claiming up to ~92% higher sequential and ~85% higher random read versus CM9. The notable detail is a deliberate split inside one product family — Gen6 / generation-10-NAND EDSFF drives versus a PCIe 5.0, generation-8-NAND 2.5-inch variant — which ServeTheHome reads as the end of roughly 15 years of 2.5-inch U.2 dominance.

insights.claim: Kioxia entered PCIe 6.0 enterprise storage ahead of FMS 2026 with the CM10 series, built on BiCS FLASH generation 10 and offering direct liquid cooling for AI infrastructure deployments.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Confirms Gen6 enterprise SSDs are arriving in the same window as Gen6 host platforms rather than lagging them.
insights.locator: Ahead of FMS 2026, Kioxia launched its new CM10 series

insights.claim: Kioxia claims the CM10 delivers up to approximately 92 percent higher sequential read and up to approximately 85 percent higher random read performance than the prior CM9 generation.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: A near-doubling of read performance per generation is the yardstick for judging competing Gen6 enterprise drives.
insights.quote: with Kioxia claiming up to approximately 92 percent higher sequential read performance and up to approximately 85 percent higher random read performance
insights.locator: Kioxia CM10 Series Specifications and Features

insights.claim: The performance jump is framed as a response to AI models approaching trillions of parameters and context windows expanding to millions of tokens.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Ties enterprise SSD spec escalation directly to model context growth, a demand driver independent of GPU unit counts.
insights.quote: These improvements address the scaling demands of AI models approaching trillions of parameters and context windows expanding to millions of tokens.
insights.locator: Kioxia CM10 Series Specifications and Features

insights.claim: Kioxia is shipping two technology levels under one product family: EDSFF models use BiCS FLASH generation 10 with PCIe 6.0, while the 2.5-inch variant uses BiCS FLASH generation 8 TLC with PCIe 5.0 compliance.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Legacy-chassis buyers get older NAND and an older interface under the same brand, so specify by form factor rather than model name.
insights.quote: the 2.5″ is listed as using BiCS FLASH generation 8 TLC flash memory with PCIe 5.0 compliance, rather than the Gen 10 memory and PCIe 6.0 interface found in EDSFF models
insights.locator: KIOXIA CM10 Series 2.5-inch PCIe NVMe specifications

insights.claim: The electrical requirements of PCIe Gen6 are pushing traditional U.2/U.3 2.5-inch drives aside in favor of EDSFF connectors, ending roughly a decade and a half of 2.5-inch U.2 dominance in NVMe SSDs.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: A connector and chassis transition with a long tail of component winners; EDSFF backplane and connector suppliers gain share.
insights.quote: Perhaps most notable is that we are finally seeing a split in NVMe SSDs away from around a decade and a half of 2.5″ U.2 form factors leading the way.

insights.claim: Pairing older NAND generations with PCIe Gen5 drives and newer NAND with Gen6 drives may become an industry-wide pattern rather than a Kioxia one-off.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: If it generalizes, older NAND nodes get a longer commercial life via Gen5 SKUs, supporting utilization of depreciated fab capacity.
insights.quote: Perhaps we will see more of that with PCIe Gen5 drives using older NAND generations, while Gen6 drives use newer ones.

insights.claim: The CM10 EDSFF lineup spans E3.S at 7.5 mm and E1.S at 9.5 mm and 15 mm, with the 9.5 mm variants of both supporting direct-cold-plate liquid cooling while all forms stay air-cooling compatible.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Liquid-cooling support is gated to specific thickness profiles, a practical constraint on retrofitting existing racks.
insights.locator: KIOXIA offers the CM10 series across multiple form factors

insights.claim: Kioxia retains dual-port designs in both the E3.S and the 2.5-inch CM10 variants to serve high-availability traditional storage arrays.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Signals Kioxia is not abandoning the classic HA enterprise array market even as it chases AI storage tiers.
insights.locator: There is also a dual-port design in E3.S

insights.claim: The Kioxia CM10 is expected to land in AI storage tiers where ephemeral KV cache exploits flash latency sitting between GPU HBM and networked storage.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Positions enterprise flash as an HBM-offload layer, a demand pool that scales with inference context length rather than GPU count alone.

insights.claim: Direct liquid-cooling capability is aimed at thermal constraints in dense GPU pods where KV cache storage is placed adjacent to accelerator racks.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Liquid-cooled SSDs extend the liquid-cooling supply chain beyond GPUs into storage, widening that component TAM.
insights.quote: Direct liquid-cooling capability addresses thermal constraints in dense GPU pods, where KV cache storage sits adjacent to accelerator racks.

insights.claim: The CM10 launch is timed to the arrival of the NVIDIA Vera CPU and the AMD EPYC Venice series, tying enterprise SSD refresh cycles to the Gen6 host platform ramp.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Gen6 SSD volume should track Gen6 CPU platform shipments; Venice and Vera ramp rates are the leading indicator.
insights.locator: Still, the new announcement is important
